diseases.name: Pre-renal acute kidney injury
diseases.inv: Urea, creatinine, potassium, urine sodium; assess volume status.

diseases.name: Intrinsic acute kidney injury (e.g. ATN, glomerulonephritis)
Chronic kidney disease
diseases.inv: Creatinine/eGFR, urine albumin-creatinine ratio, ultrasound kidneys.

diseases.name: Ureteric / renal stone
diseases.inv: Non-contrast CT KUB or ultrasound, urine routine, creatinine.

diseases.name: Urinary tract cancer (bladder/kidney)
diseases.inv: Urine cytology, ultrasound, cystoscopy, CT urography.

diseases.name: Glomerulonephritis
diseases.inv: Urine microscopy, protein, creatinine, ASO titre, complement; BP.

diseases.name: Acute pyelonephritis
diseases.inv: Urine culture, CBC, creatinine, blood cultures if septic; ultrasound.

diseases.name: Sexually transmitted urethritis
diseases.inv: Gram stain/NAAT, STI screen, HIV and syphilis testing.

diseases.name: Leaking aortic aneurysm
diseases.inv: Emergency senior and vascular review, bedside ultrasound.

diseases.name: Benign prostatic enlargement
diseases.inv: Prostate examination, PSA counselling, ultrasound, creatinine.
diseases.tool: IPSS scores symptom severity; it is not diagnostic.

diseases.name: Hypertensive emergency
diseases.inv: Urgent assessment for organ damage: ECG, creatinine, urine, fundoscopy, neurology.
diseases.alt: Acute coronary syndrome, stroke, aortic dissection

diseases.name: Phaeochromocytoma
diseases.inv: Plasma or urinary metanephrines, then imaging.

diseases.name: Secondary hypertension (renal, endocrine)
diseases.inv: Creatinine, electrolytes, urine tests, renal ultrasound, aldosterone-renin ratio as indicated.

diseases.name: Primary (essential) hypertension
diseases.inv: Repeat BP measurements, ECG, creatinine, glucose, lipids, urine.
diseases.tool: Use national or ESC/AHA hypertension guidelines for thresholds.

flags.text: Reduced urine with dehydration or kidney-risk exposure: possible acute kidney injury, check creatinine and potassium
Urinary symptoms with fever and rigors: possible pyelonephritis/urosepsis, assess urgently
Sudden severe flank/back pain with faintness in an older vascular patient: possible aortic aneurysm leak, emergency
Very high BP with severe symptoms: possible hypertensive emergency
